answer: Persistent work ledger with non-transferable history. Each identity must solve a distinct random challenge, a cipher tied to prior ledger entries, before its first transaction, so clones pay full compute per identity while sharing no history. A clone’s marginal revenue stays zero because counterparties weight reputation by a vertex in the trust graph that cannot be forged without that history, and the lagoon of idle identities earns nothing. The attacker pays one full proof-of-work sequence plus ongoing storage per clone, making each addition strictly negative-EV.
